rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one binds more forcefully than the zabāniya bind those who disbelieved in their Lord; this concerns the criminal and unjust among creatures.
rows.anchor: ليس أحد أشد قبضا ووثقا من الزبانية لمن كفر بربهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one binds more forcefully than the zabāniya bind those who disbelieved in their Lord; this concerns the criminal and unjust among creatures.
rows.anchor: ليس أحد أشد قبضا ووثقا من الزبانية لمن كفر بربهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one binds more forcefully than the zabāniya bind those who disbelieved in their Lord; this concerns the criminal and unjust among creatures.
rows.anchor: ليس أحد أشد قبضا ووثقا من الزبانية لمن كفر بربهم

rows.speaker: مجاهد والحسن وقتادة والسدي وغيرهم
rows.claim: They understand lubadan as a great deal: Adam's son boasts that he spent much money.
rows.anchor: قاله مجاهد [ والحسن ]

rows.speaker: مجاهد وغيره من السلف
rows.claim: The one who sees the person is God; other early authorities gave the same interpretation.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد : أي أيحسب أن لم يره الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made him two eyes with which to see.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { أَلَمْ نَجْعَلْ لَهُ عَيْنَيْنِ } أي : يبصر بهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sūrat al-Layl is Meccan.
rows.anchor:
تفسير سورة الليل
وهي مكية .

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir recalls the Prophet asking Muʿadh why he had not prayed using al-Aʿlā, al-Shams and al-Layl.
rows.anchor: قوله عليه الصلاة والسلام لمعاذ :  " فهلا صليت ب "

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود وأبو الدرداء عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd read wa-l-dhakari wa-l-unthā; Abū al-Dardāʾ affirmed that he heard the Prophet recite this form.
rows.anchor: فقال أبو الدرداء : لقد سمعتها من رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read the wording found in the Uthmanic muṣḥaf used across the regions.
rows.anchor: وأما الجمهور فقرأوا ذلك كما هو مثبت في المصحف الإمام العثماني في سائر الآفاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God swears by night covering creation in darkness, day appearing with light, and the creation of male and female, as in 78:8 and 51:49.
rows.anchor: فأقسم تعالى ب { وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَى } أي : إذا غشي الخليقة بظلامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oaths name opposites, matching the contrast among people's acquired deeds: some do good and others evil.
rows.anchor: ولما كان القسم بهذه الأشياء المتضادة كان القسم عليه أيضا متضادا ؛ ولهذا قال : { إِنَّ سَعْيَكُمْ لَشَتَّى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The giver gives what he has been commanded to give and fears God in his affairs.
rows.anchor: أي : أعطى ما أمر بإخراجه ،   واتقى الله في أموره

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada understands al-ḥusnā as recompense for the giving and piety just mentioned.
rows.anchor: بالمجازاة على ذلك - قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: خصيف
rows.claim: Khasif interprets al-ḥusnā as the reward.
rows.anchor: على ذلك - قاله قتادة ،   وقال خصيف : بالثواب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وعكرمة وأبو صالح وزيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: These authorities interpret al-ḥusnā as replacement or compensation.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس ،   ومجاهد ،   وعكرمة ،   وأبو صالح ،   وزيد بن أسلم

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي والضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Sulami and al-Dahhak interpret al-ḥusnā as the testimony lā ilāha illā Allāh.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي ،   والضحاك

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: In one narration from ʿIkrima, al-ḥusnā means what God bestowed upon the person.
rows.anchor: وفي رواية عن عكرمة : { وَصَدَّقَ بِالْحُسْنَى } أي : بما أنعم الله عليه

rows.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: In one narration Zayd ibn Aslam interprets al-ḥusnā as prayer, alms, and fasting.
rows.anchor: وفي رواية عن زيد بن أسلم : { وَصَدَّقَ بِالْحُسْنَى } قال : الصلاة والزكاة والصوم

rows.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam also gave the interpretation of the obligatory charity at the end of Ramadan.
rows.anchor: وفي رواية عن زيد بن أسلم : { وَصَدَّقَ بِالْحُسْنَى } قال : الصلاة والزكاة والصوم .   وقال مرة : وصدقة الفطر

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Asked by Ubayy ibn Kaʿb about al-ḥusnā, the Prophet answered that it is Paradise; Ibn Kathir gives no grading here.
rows.anchor: عن أبي بن كعب قال : سألت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الحسنى قال : " الحسنى : الجنة "

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says being made ready for al-yusrā means being directed toward good.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : يعني للخير

rows.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam says al-yusrā means Paradise.
rows.anchor: وقال زيد بن أسلم : يعني للجنة

rows.speaker: بعض السلف
rows.claim: Some early authorities say one reward of a good deed is the good deed that follows, and one punishment of sin is the sin that follows; Ibn Kathir links this to the next clause.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض السلف : من ثواب الحسنة

rows.speaker: عكرمة عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, as relayed by ʿIkrima, explains that the person withholds his wealth and considers himself independent of his Lord.
rows.anchor: قال عكرمة ،   عن ابن عباس : أي بخل بماله ،   واستغنى عن ربه ،   عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here al-ḥusnā is the recompense in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: أي : بالجزاء في الدار الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿusrā means the path of evil; Ibn Kathir compares this divine turning of hearts to 6:110.
rows.anchor: أي : لطريق الشر ،   كما قال تعالى : { وَنُقَلِّبُ أَفْئِدَتَهُمْ وَأَبْصَارَهُمْ

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid interprets the moment of falling as the person's death.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد : أي إذا مات

rows.speaker: أبو صالح ومالك عن زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: Abu Salih and Malik, reporting from Zayd ibn Aslam, interpret it as falling into the Fire.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو صالح ،   ومالك عن زيد بن أسلم : إذا تردى في النار

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says God undertakes to make the lawful and unlawful clear.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة : { إِنَّ عَلَيْنَا لَلْهُدَى } أي : نبين الحلال والحرام

rows.speaker: غيره، حكاه ابن جرير
rows.claim: Another interpretation says whoever follows the path of guidance reaches God, likening it to 16:9.
rows.anchor: وقال غيره : من سلك طريق الهدى وصل إلى الله . وجعله كقوله تعالى : { وَعَلَى اللَّهِ قَصْدَ السَّبِيلِ }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both the Hereafter and the present world belong to God, and He directs them.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { وَإِنَّ لَنَا لَلآخِرَةَ وَالأولَى } أي : الجميع ملكنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only the most wretched enters the Fire in a way that surrounds him on every side.
rows.anchor: أي : لا يدخلها دخولا يحيط به من جميع جوانبه إلا الأشقى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person denies with his heart and turns away by refusing action through his limbs and bodily faculties.
rows.anchor: أي : بقلبه ،   { وَتَوَلَّى } أي : عن العمل بجوارحه وأركانه

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says only a wretched person enters the Fire, defining that person as one who neither obeys God nor leaves a sin for His sake.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : " لا يدخل النار إلا شقي " . قيل : ومن الشقي ؟ قال : " الذي لا يعمل بطاعة ،   ولا يترك لله معصية "

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says his community will enter Paradise except those who refuse: whoever obeys him enters it, and whoever disobeys has refused.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : " كل أمتي تدخل الجنة يوم القيامة إلا من أبى "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pure, God-fearing person will be moved far away from the Fire.
rows.anchor: أي : وسيزحزح عن النار التقي النقي الأتقى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He spends wealth in obedience to his Lord, purifying himself, his wealth, and what God granted him in religion and worldly life.
rows.anchor: أي : يصرف ماله في طاعة ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sūrat al-Ḍuḥā is Meccan.
rows.anchor:
تفسير سورة الضحى
وهي مكية .

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A recitation practice reported through al-Bazzī's chain instructs takbīr at the end of each sūra and traces through Ibn Kathīr, Mujāhid, Ibn ʿAbbās and Ubayy to the Prophet; Ibn Kathir says al-Bazzī alone transmitted it.
rows.anchor: وأخبره أبي أنه قرأ على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فأمره بذلك

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن البزي
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir says this takbīr practice was uniquely transmitted by al-Bazzī, an imam in Qurʾānic readings.
rows.anchor: فهذه سنة تفرد بها أبو الحسن أحمد بن محمد بن عبد الله البزي ،   من ولد القاسم

rows.speaker: أبو حاتم الرازي وأبو جعفر العقيلي
rows.claim: Abu Hatim weakened al-Bazzī and refused to narrate from him; al-ʿUqaylī also called him munkar al-ḥadīth.
rows.anchor: فأما في الحديث فقد ضعفه أبو حاتم الرازي وقال : لا أحدث عنه ،   وكذلك أبو جعفر العقيلي قال : هو منكر الحديث

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Abu Shama relates that al-Shafiʿī praised hearing the takbīr in prayer as doing well and following the Sunnah, which supports the report's authenticity.
rows.anchor: حكى الشيخ شهاب الدين أبو شامة في شرح الشاطبية عن الشافعي أنه سمع رجلا يكبر هذا التكبير في الصلاة ،   فقال له : أحسنت وأصبت السنة

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some reciters begin the takbīr at the end of Sūrat al-Layl.
rows.anchor: فقال بعضهم : يكبر من آخر

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Other reciters begin the takbīr at the end of Sūrat al-Ḍuḥā.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون : من آخر

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some reciters say only Allāhu akbar.
rows.anchor: وكيفية التكبير عند بعضهم أن يقول : الله أكبر ويقتصر

rows.speaker: ومنهم
rows.claim: Other reciters use the longer formula Allāhu akbar, there is no god but God, and God is greatest.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من يقول الله أكبر ،   لا إله إلا الله والله أكبر

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ suggested that after revelation resumed following a pause, the Prophet joyfully said takbīr; Ibn Kathir says al-Farrāʾ supplied no isnād that could be judged sound or weak.
rows.anchor: وذكر الفراء في مناسبة التكبير من أول سورة

rows.speaker: جندب عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Jundub reports that after the Prophet was ill and missed prayer for one or two nights, a woman said his Satan had left him, and God revealed al-Ḍuḥā and the following reassurance.
rows.anchor: عن الأسود بن قيس قال : سمعت جندبا يقول : اشتكى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فلم يقم ليلة أو ليلتين

rows.speaker: جندب عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: In another narration, Gabriel was delayed and the polytheists said Muhammad had been abandoned; the revelation answered them that his Lord had not abandoned or detested him.
rows.anchor: وفي رواية سفيان بن عيينة عن الأسود بن قيس : سمع جندبا قال : أبطأ جبريل على رسول الله

rows.speaker: جندب
rows.claim: A report says a stone cut the Prophet's finger; after he did not rise for two or three nights, a woman said his Satan had left him, then the sūra was revealed.
rows.anchor: أنه سمع جندبا يقول : رمي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بحجر في أصبعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir says the poetic line about the Prophet's bleeding finger is authentic in both Ṣaḥīḥ collections, but calls it unusual to make the injury the cause of his missed prayers and the sūra's revelation.
rows.anchor: ولكن الغريب هاهنا جعله سببا لتركه القيام ،   ونزول هذه السورة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One account identifies the woman who said the Prophet's Satan had left him as Umm Jamīl, the wife of Abū Lahab.
rows.anchor: قيل : إن هذه المرأة هي : أم جميل امرأة أبي لهب

rows.speaker: خديجة
rows.claim: Two reports from Ibn Jarīr say Khadīja told the Prophet that she thought his Lord had forsaken him; Ibn Kathir notes both are mursal and suggests her attribution may be unpreserved or an expression of sorrow.
rows.anchor: ولعل ذكر خديجة ليس محفوظا ،   أو قالته على وجه التأسف والتحزن

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق وبعض السلف
rows.claim: Some early authorities, including Ibn Isḥāq, say this was the sūra Gabriel revealed when he appeared in his created form and descended to the Prophet at al-Abṭaḥ, as in 53:10.
rows.anchor: وقد ذكر بعض السلف - منهم ابن إسحاق - أن هذه السورة هي التي أوحاها جبريل إلى رسول الله

rows.speaker: العوفي عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-ʿAwfī reports from Ibn ʿAbbās that when revelation paused for days and polytheists said God had abandoned and detested Muhammad, this reassurance was revealed.
rows.anchor: قال العوفي ،   عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God swears by the forenoon and the light placed within it.
rows.anchor: وهذا قسم منه تعالى بالضحى وما جعل فيه من الضياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir says Muhammad's father died while he was still in his mother's womb.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن أباه توفي وهو حمل في بطن أمه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternate report says Muhammad's father died after he was born.
rows.anchor: وقيل : بعد أن ولد ،   عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His mother Āmina died when he was six; his grandfather ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib cared for him until age eight, after which his uncle Abū Ṭālib took charge.
rows.anchor: ثم توفيت أمه آمنة بنت وهب وله من العمر ست سنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ṭālib supported and protected him after prophethood despite remaining an idolater; after his death shortly before the Hijra, God brought about the move to the Anṣār, who sheltered, defended and fought for him, all as divine care.
rows.anchor: فكفله عمه أبو طالب . ثم لم يزل يحوطه وينصره ويرفع من قدره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir links the phrase to 42:52: Muhammad did not know the Book or faith until revelation was made a light by which God guides and he guides to a straight path.
rows.anchor: كقوله { وَكَذَلِكَ أَوْحَيْنَا إِلَيْكَ رُوحًا مِنْ أَمْرِنَا

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say Muhammad was lost among the ravines of Mecca as a child, then found his way back.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من قال [ إن ]

rows.speaker: قيل، حكاه البغوي
rows.claim: Another account says that while traveling to Syria with his uncle, Muhammad's camel was diverted at night by Iblis; Gabriel blew Iblis away toward Abyssinia and guided the mount back to the road.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إنه ضل وهو مع عمه في طريق الشام ،   وكان راكبا ناقة في الليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad was poor and had dependents, then God enriched him so he needed no one else; this joined patient poverty with grateful wealth.
rows.anchor: أي : كنت فقيرا ذا عيال ،   فأغناك الله عمن سواه ،   فجمع له بين مقامي ،   الفقير الصابر والغني الشاكر

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says these three conditions were the Messenger's circumstances before God sent him as a prophet.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة في قوله : { أَلَمْ يَجِدْكَ يَتِيمًا فَآوَى

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet teaches that true richness is richness of the soul rather than having many worldly goods.
rows.anchor: عن همام بن منبه قال : هذا ما حدثنا أبو هريرة قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : " ليس الغنى عن كثرة العرض

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says successful is the one who submits, receives enough, and is made content by God with what he has been given.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمرو قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : " قد أفلح من أسلم
